text_fidelity_a: Franklin Sports Mini Putt Golf Game for Kids - Spin n' Putt Electronic Putting Game - Indoor Mini Golf for Kids + Toddlers - Putter + Balls Included The Franklin spin n putt golf game is a pretty cool game. There are 10 holes/slots for the golf balls to land in with points ranging from 5 to 100. 5 of the 10 balls are white and the other 5 are yellow. Once you decide who goes first he or she will putt all 5 balls toward the base. Anything not in a slot counts as 0 points. After player one shoots player 2 gets to shoot his or her 5 balls. Clearly, you are able to make up your own game and rules.  The one thing I like about this set is that there is no putting green strip. Therefore you are able to putt from any angle or even try to bounce off a wall and into the slots. If you had a putting green strip this type of play would not be easy because you would have to roll up and over the edge of the green. Cool game.  Made in China.

text_fidelity_a:
Sunny Health & Fitness Twisting Stair Stepper Machine with Handlebar and Digital Display This just arrived so it's too soon to say, but I REALLY miss my Aspen stepper that lasted forever and would probably still be going strong if I hadn't lent it to my kids who left it out in the rain and ruined it.

PROS: It was relatively easy to assemble; it's made of steel rather than plastic; it has a built in timer (also a scan, calorie counter and stroke counter), but the accuracy of these things is dubious at best, and I'm not one to use them anyway; it doesn't take up much space and is easy to move.

CONS: The tension adjustment knob is a joke. From the easiest to the most difficult setting is so subtle, I barely noticed it. Even at the most difficult setting, going as fast as I could, I didn't perspire at all; for people who are used to steppers, the twisting motion is a bit awkward, and since it came with no exercise instructions, perhaps there's something I'm missing to the advantages of twisting; at full extension, the handle bars don't go up very high, and they don't move.

If you're someone just embarking on an exercise routine, don't want to spend a lot of money and don't have a lot of space, this will probably work just fine. However, for the athletically inclined who already work out regularly, this will probably be a bit of a disappointment.

Update: Have now had this for a while and need to mention that 1) the tension adjustment knob does work but ONLY WORKS IF YOU LET THE STEPPER SIT FOR AT LEAST A COUPLE OF HOURS. If you try adjusting it without letting is sit undisturbed, you will NOT feel any difference; and 2) the 250# weight limit is a joke. My husband, who weighs 195, can't use it at all. If he does, the cable screws (as others have commented) break off. He's handy, so he's been able to fix it each time, but after 3 or 4 times, he just will no longer use it. For me, it's not much of a work out, but I do use it.

Update a little over a year later: The cable broke, and the manufacturer has been unresponsive. So into the trash it sadly goes. Due to a major design flaw in construction, the cable is forced to stretch, wear down and eventually break with use over time. A hydraulic resistance system would be a major design improvement. So if you don't mind a machine that will only last about a year, this stepper is fine. But if you want something that will last longer, I'd give it a miss.
text_fidelity_b: Sunny Health & Fitness Twisting Stair Stepper Machine with Handlebar and Digital Display

text_fidelity_a:
CAT EYE, Strada Cadence Wired Bike Computer - Took me about 45 min to get it setup. You need lots of patience. Easier to install if bike on trainer so pedals and rear wheel move freely.
- you need to tell the computer the circumference of your tires. My tire size 700x45 was not listed on the chart in the instructions. It was listed on the chart on the cateye website - 2242.
- No tools except scissors to cut ends of zip ties (after everything is lined up and working). I also used black electrical tape to hold sensors in place while lining everything up.
-Important tip: Don’t tighten any zip ties until you are sure everything is lined up and working.
- It seems to be functioning correctly. Not sure if its accurate?? Wont be able to tell until I ride outside and compare it to my mapmyride app. Its one of the only computers I found that works with a trainer and is relatively inexpensive. $47.
To install:
- You need to put a magnet on a wheel spoke on back wheel and then attach a sensor to the bike chain stay. They have to be < 3 mm apart.
- You then need to put a magnet on the crank arm thats attached to the pedal and a sensor on the bike chain stay thats < 3 mm apart. You have to use a zip tie to attach the magnet. My pedal crank arm has an indentation in it, so i had to tape the zip tie to the bar so it doesn't slide around.
- You then take the wire attached to both sensors and attach it to the bike from the pedal up to the handle bars. You need to make sure the wire is attached so when you move the handle bars to turn the wheel, the wire is long enough and it doesn't tear or get caught.
- they included 10 zip ties. I used 9 of them. You need lots of patience to get it setup correctly. The magnets have to be lined up exactly with the sensors. There is a line on each sensor showing you where to line up the magnets. Its near the ends of the sensors not the middle.
- I have numerous items on my handlebars already - phone holder, bell, reflector, a mount for a computer. I attached this device to the computer mount but this computer is very small so its not a great fit. I had to wrap the strap around the mount.
- if you snap the computer onto the holder at the end of the wire, you can unattach it, but its very hard to do. Beware. You need to pull up on front of the computer while pushing back on it. I was afraid I was breaking it or would tear the wire away from the holder. I have done it several times to test it, and it’s still working.
I’m giving this a 4 star review pending longer term use. If it turns out to be accurate and lasts, I will bump it up to a 5 star.
text_fidelity_b: CAT EYE, Strada Cadence Wired Bike Computer

It's a good uphill cardio workout, strengthens the quads and glutes and helps get rid of some of those extra butt-cheeks. text_fidelity_a:
The Omega Project Black Book Training Journal – US Army Special Operations Elite Workout Planner – Leather Fitness Tracker Notebook Logs Exercise, Sleep, Recovery, Nutrition and More I like this nutrition journal because it addresses unhealthy attitudes about food. Because it is based in a cognitive behavioral therapy approach, it really comes down to values. Do I value my life more than I value instant gratification? Am I living my values? This method doesn't preach nor are the expectations too vigorous as I can modify the exercise to take into account my disability and nutritional requirements. It approaches nutrition, body composition, and the mental attitudes that lead to unhealthy eating as simply as can be. But at no time is it turning a deaf ear to how difficult it can be to actually make changes. That's why the journalling is so important. Further, you can customize for yourself your physical ability or dietary needs. It isn't really about if you can run a mile in 5 minutes, but about whether you take a step towards your goal.

As adults, we are all responsible for our choices and for what we do with our lives. Maybe it isn't my fault that I have an unhealthy attitude towards food, but it is each of our responsibility to love ourselves enough to be willing to change. This journal is not going to magically fix 30 years of unhealthy thinking or eating. What it can do is to start a question in your brain about what do you value, what can motivate you to take those steps towards healthy behaviors. I don't have to feel bad about not biking a hundred miles a day; I just have to love myself enough to make decisions that will lead to healthier behaviors. This journal is a good step towards my goals.
text_fidelity_b: The Omega Project Black Book Training Journal – US Army Special Operations Elite Workout Planner – Leather Fitness Tracker Notebook Logs Exercise, Sleep, Recovery, Nutrition and More

Pflueger President Spinning Reel, Fishing Reel, Right/Left Handle Position, Graphite Body and Rotor, Corrosion-Resistant, Aluminum Spool, Front Drag System I can't say enough about this reel. I don't have a lot of money, but I love to fish. One day I decided I was going to treat myself and buy a $150 reel. I spent any hour and a half in Cabela's and about the same at Sportsman's. I tried every reel in the place, and still ended up with the Pres 30. It's just the best feeling reel I've ever used, and I've borrowed plenty over my 40+ years.

But it's not just great to play with in the store. I've caught probably 200 trout on mine, and it's been beat up. Dropped, submerged, dragged through mud, and covered in clay. I treated it the same way I did my Abu ProMax, and that piece of garbage died after 2 months.

If you're looking for a great reel and you have $150 to spend, get this and use the extra money to buy a nice rod, some good copoly line, and gas up your truck. Go fish!

text_fidelity_a:
Chef'sChoice Knife Sharpener (Discontinued by Manufacturer) We have three sets of kitchen knives; a low quality TV infomercial special, a medium quality Chicago Cutlery set, and what we consider high quality home knives by J.A. Henckels. Plus we have more working knives than I care to count. I have used a lot of sharpeners and edge straighteners over the decades but we only use those now for machetes that my wife won't let me use in the Chef's Choice 120. They'd fit too!

I bought the 120 for my wife two years after I bought her the J.A. Henckels knives. New, the knives were amazing; felt like they had a near surgical edge. I knew once they got dull or burred we didn't have anything that would restore them to like-new condition. Before we bought the 120 we took our dull Chicago Cutlery knives to a professional butcher for sharpening to see what we'd get back. We were not impressed with the results so I knew we needed to find a good knife sharpener.

After reading the reviews on sharpeners, I chose the Chef's Choice 120. We carefully read the directions and practiced our technique on the cheap knives. Wow, talk about impressed with the results. Then we put the dull Chicago Cutlery knives through all three stages on the 120. Several of the knives were so dull we had to three-stage them three times to recover the edge. When we were finished they sliced effortlessly through paper! They had NEVER been that sharp, even new. They are decades old knives and I will admit the 1st stage of the 120 did put some scratches on the blades about 1/4" up from the edge, but we didn't care. We just wanted a razor sharp edge on the old knives and the 120 delivered.

We tested stage two and three on some loose knives we had to see if those stages scratched the knife blade. They didn't. Most knives that are maintained properly only require stage two and three, or only stage 3. Once we were confident of no scratches we used only the Stage 3 polishing strop stage on the newer J.A. Henckels. Although the knives were two years old and still exceptionally sharp, they had not been sharpened since we bought them. Plus they had developed a few small burrs. The 120 Stage 3 strop stage removed the burrs, restored the near surgical, like-new edge, and no scratches either. My wife was thrilled with the results!

We use the Stage 3 strop stage on several serrated knives we own and they are noticeably improved and shaper. I've used the 120 on my working pocket knives too. I thought they were acceptably sharp using a diamond edge straightener but the 120 takes sharpening to a completely new level.

The 120 will get hot sharpening a bunch of knives one right after the other, but we typically limit our sharpening to ten knives or less. Stage 1 definitely does scratch the blade but that stage is only recommended for hopelessly dull knives.

Others may have issues with the 120. Not us. Once you understand the technique you need to use with the sharpener, it works great! We love it!

text_fidelity_a:
King Koil Twin Air Mattress with Built-in Pump - Double High Elevated Raised Airbed for Guests with Comfortable Top Inflatable Bed with 1-Year Guarantee from The Manufacturer This mattress looked great out of the box. Now less than ten days later it's on its way to the garbage bin.

It looked good at first. The material seemed high-quality and the built-in pump worked great to inflate it, relatively quickly. I went online while the mattress was inflating and read all of the manufacturer's suggestions, including the one to inflate it and let it sit overnight before use to "stretch out", then add more air. I followed all the instructions carefully.

Just a few hours after fully inflating the mattress and without anyone using it or even sitting on it, I pressed on it with my hand and noticed it was already mushy and not nearly as firm as when first inflated, so I topped the air off again and let it sit overnight without using it. The next morning it was mushy again, but I figured maybe this was the "stretching" the manufacturer was talking about. That night I inflated the mattress to full firmness, made up the bed, and went to sleep. About three hours later I woke up with the hard floor under me and a tangle of deflated air mattress wrapped around me.

So clearly, the mattress was defective and had arrived with a leak. Well, that happens. It was really unfortunate because I had no other bed at the time to use, but I had gotten a cheerful email from the manufacturer here on Amazon right after I ordered, telling me if I had any problems to contact them and they would be sure to honor that warranty twhich hey make such a big deal of offering, and make things right.

I emailed them to let them know that right out of the box the mattress was leaking air badly. They replied with the same instructions I found online, saying it was probably "stretching out" and I just needed to top the air off. I replied that I had now spent two nights on the mattress, and the only way to use it was to set an alarm to wake up every two-and-a-half hours to reinflate it before it went completely flat. I asked them to please do as they said and work with me to make it right.

That more than a week and three emails ago. I have emailed them over and over (the only way to reach them.) The manufacturer simply stopped responding after the first email. They did not provide any customer support, no advice, nothing. They did nothing at all to honor the warranty they offer. I tried finding a patch kit on my own for this thing, but I can't even find the leak, it seems to be in the sealing of one of the seams. It's basically garbage at this point, because it's useless. The photo is of it sitting waiting to go out with the trash less than two weeks after being bought.

If you look at the one and two star reviews, many people have had the same issue. With this mattress, it seems like either you are one of the lucky ones and it works perfectly out of the box, or it just doesn't hold air at all and you are screwed, because the manufacturer is not going to keep their word and honor that reassuring-sounding warranty that they offer to entice people into buying their expensive air mattress.

So, if you need a bed and want to roll the dice, try your luck. I did, and I certainly regret believing the untrustworthy, dishonorable shysters who manufacture the King Koil.

$150 dollars, straight out into the trash.
text_fidelity_b: King Koil Twin Air Mattress with Built-in Pump - Double High Elevated Raised Airbed for Guests with Comfortable Top Inflatable Bed with 1-Year Guarantee from The Manufacturer

text_fidelity_a:
Mother Earth Products Zucchini, Quart Jar, 8 oz Pointing out a few things brought up in reviews:

1. This is DEHYDRATED zucchini, NOT freeze-dried. Very different methods, different results, different pricing. While Mother Earth does carry some freeze dried, they do not have freeze dried zucchini. Another way to tell? With freeze dried foods, they can be eaten as is (crunchy snack) or rehydrated. Where as with dehydrated foods, most all (except fruits, usually) will need to be rehydrated in order to consume them (too tough to eat). This will require soaking and/or cooking for a period of time. Can't just toss it in the dish you are making and expect it to cook up quickly. So for this, it says to simmer 1 part zucchini to 2 parts water for 10-30 minutes. This very well may take longer. I let it cook for no less than 30 minutes before adding it to what I ultimately want to have it be part of. Another way to get it started is to let soak, then follow up with a shorter simmer.

2. 1/2 cup dried zucchini = 1 cup cooked zucchini. I made up 1/4 cup and it made a very good sized portion. See my pics.

3. End result is NOT EVER going to be same as fresh. Stop that. Then stop blaming the company/brand. YOu will always be disappointed. Best thing to get if you cant get fresh or frozen is to find a company who makes freeze dried. Even then, you are expecting a lot from zucchini. This is similar to others, and there aren't many out there to choose from.

4. Shelf life can be very very long, if not indefinite if stored under proper conditions. Freeze dried for sure, but dehydrated can last a very long time. Be sure to keep it in well sealed container, out of light and dampness. Maybe keep in freezer or further repackaged into mylar or vac sealed jar.

5. Taste is neutral. Kind of like how zucchini can be. I could tell it was zucchini though! I found that with proper rehydration it worked well in adding bulk to tacos, and can always be added to soup. I see it as a nutritional item rather than a way to have a plate of zucchini. Nice way to bulk up meals, add vitamins and minerals, yet not have to rely on fresh (for various reasons). I noticed that the skins were more like late summer yellow squash/zucchini. Kinda reminded me of regular squash- like butternut skins. Not tough but had more "presence" I shall say. DID not taste or feel like "tree bark" in any way.

6. If planning on using it in zucchini bread, muffins, cookies, or sauces, I would recommend running it through the blender after it has been rehydrated. Make it more of a puree. This will impart flavor and decrease any tougher bits.

7. Says processed and packaged in USA, but WHERE do they get their vegetables from?? That I havent seen, here or on their web page

8. If you dont like this packaging, they also offer mylar bag style.

OVERALL: I think it is fine, and it as expected. I love seeing it in my pantry knowing that I have a variety of dehydrated foods to use when I cant get fresh, or food is scarce, or food doesnt look good, or I cant afford it that day. Buy a little here and there and stock up those cupboards. Would like to know where the zucchini comes from?

PS. I miss when we could comment and ask questions of other reviewers. One person just said "poisonous". Like, what do they even mean by that? I had this a few times and doing well so far :)
text_fidelity_b: Mother Earth Products Zucchini, Quart Jar, 8 oz

I agree with the other review that says that this coffee press is cheaply made. I bought it because the carafe part is plastic and resistant to breakage when camping. The plunger part is where the cheap manufacturing shows: the wire mesh and spring are crude, compared to the Bodum. But, the worst part is that the various pieces of the plunger are held together by a plastic cap that comes loose (after only about 10 uses), allowing the mesh screen to slip upwards along the shaft of the plunger, resulting in a press that can't press at all.

I suppose I could fix this with a stainless steel nut, washer and collet rig-up, but the point is the design and manufacture of a product should give it a reasonable life expectancy.

text_fidelity_a:
Madd Gear VX7 Mini Pro This scooter is slightly smaller than other "pro" scooters that accommodate teens and adults. My 9 year old has ridden the larger scooters and didn't seem to have a problem, but is more comfortable with the slightly lower and narrower bars on this scooter. The deck is a little narrower too, but still about the same width as a Razr A (but much shorter)

The scooter is built like a "pro" scooter, with a extruded deck, welded truss to the headstock which has a high-tensile (not chromoly) steel fork, a Internal Hidden Compression (IHC) headset which is the same as "HIC." The bars are chromoly (not aluminum). After getting the bars clamped on, a drop test showed this scooter is "dialed."

Here's a few shortcomings: The brake is composite (plastic) instead of steel. The fork is hi-ten steel instead of chromoly or 6061 Aluminum. The bars are chromoly which might be heavier than Aluminum or Titanium bars but they're still awesome. These things combine to make this scooter less expensive than typical "complete" pro scooters which seem to start around one-hundred fifty dollars and go up to several hundred dollars or more.

One problem I ran into was the bar clamp was not threaded completely through. So the bolts would bottom out on on the far-side of the clamp. I couldn't tighten them any further and almost damaged them trying to. I confirmed everything else was correct by using a clamp from another scooter. Then I had to use an 8mm x 1.25 tpi tap to finish threading the clamp. Once the clamp was threaded all the way through, it clamped the bars onto the fork just fine.

Since the scooter is new, I can't comment on how the bearings and wheels hold up yet. So far, so good.
text_fidelity_b: Madd Gear VX7 Mini Pro

text_fidelity_a:
AMNQUERXUS Machine Washable Reflective Running Vest with LED Lights USB Rechargeable Safety Gear with Adjustable Waist, High Visibility Light Up Flashing Vest Gifts for Men Women Kids Dog Walking Sometimes where we live, it can get really scary when people drive by quickly and you are trying to go for a walk in the country to just relax. Having this vest handy is really a great item to put on both during the night time or dusk hours, or during hunting season to keep from being shot.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
CLOSURES
This comes with an XL vest that fits around the sides and closes. with strong velcro type closures.

FABRIC
This is a very nice mesh fabric. It allows for airflow and has a slight stretch/give to it so it is comfortable.

SIZING
This fits me and I am between a size 14 and 16 misses. If I were to put this over a winter jacket, I could still close it unless the coat is WAY too puffy.

HOW DOES THIS WORK?
POWER BOX
This is ingenious, actually. There is a little packet which recharges. It has a plug on it and also a cord that is USB to recharge it. Once it is charged, then you slip the little box unto a closed pocket which sits under a power button. The box gives a place for the power button to rest on when you press it.

LIGHTS
Once you have it connected, the button is pressed once, and you get the lights on front and back to go on. Once the lights are on, then you can make them flash fast by pressing another time. One more press makes for a slower blink, and a fourth press turns them off.

VEST
The vest itself is brilliant neon yellow. There is plenty of reflective tape all over this vest front and back. There is even a zipper pocket on the front for you to put your phone or other small items in.

BATTERY LIFE?
The battery life of this seems quite good. I have used it a few times and there is still no need for a recharge. I would say you could get a few hours of continuous use at least per charge, maybe more. My outings did not add up to that much yet.

WASHING
I am only going to handwash this without the battery pack and air dry it well before trying to use again. It will dry fast due to the fabric.

HUNTING SEASON
Around my area, fall time into winter can be dangerous. We have had our home shot by hunters by accident, and often there are inexperienced people who try to hunt and they don't pay attention to what is going on, thinking noises are deer. This vest will alert anyone in the early morning or early evening hours that there is a person there.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a great vest to have handy. I plan to keep using this especially through hunting season and for late night walks when i hear a car coming.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is an ingenious little invention and I am glad to have it. I am considering purchasing others for the rest of the family.
text_fidelity_b: AMNQUERXUS Machine Washable Reflective Running Vest with LED Lights USB Rechargeable Safety Gear with Adjustable Waist, High Visibility Light Up Flashing Vest Gifts for Men Women Kids Dog Walking

K-MingleSo Upgraded Portable Folding Stool, 13 Inch Camping Stool for Adults Fishing Hiking Gardening and Beach with Carry Bag, Hold Up to 450lbs[Camo] I am recovering from a walking issue. As I continue to recover, I am trying to find ways to include some easy to store stools or small places to sit if I find myself in a situation where I have to stand for too long. This looked perfect.

HOW THIS COMES
This comes all disassembled in a drawstring bag with basic instruction sheet.

HOW TO ASSEMBLE
You take the elastic loop off of the pieces. Then you quickly assemble the pieces which are shock corded together to make a nice stool.

PHONE POUCH
There is a pocket on the front that fits most phones.

WHAT'S THE PROBLEM?
I was so thrilled to get this, but when I put it together, I was not sure if I should laugh or cry. The stool is TINY. I am talking TODDLER TINY. It is not quite 12 inches off the ground and there is nothing to hold on to to get up. This is almost like sitting on the floor- not quite.

If I were to open this up and sit in public while waiting, I am sure I would like weird. It is a very tiny stool which is perfect if you are a toddler. As an adult, it is ridiculous looking.

THE BOTTOM LINE
I had high hopes for this thing. It is so ridiculously tiny that I can not use it. Maybe the cat can have it be her seat in the summer when we are camping. Maybe there is a toad that needs a chair.

MY RATING
ONE STAR. This should be pointed out to be for children or very very small people. It is not suitable for most adults I know- even older kids laughed when I showed it to them. For toddlers, I would give this four stars (because it is tough to put together for toddler ages). For adults ONE STAR.

Bonnlo Boat Kayak Canoe Cart Carrier Dolly Trailer Tote Trolley Transport Kayak Accessories Large with 20x2mm Aluminum Pipe Double Kickstands, Inflation Free Solid Tire Wheels, 2 Ratchet Straps This was pretty easy to assemble, it appears very well made. Good wheels, straps and metal.

No matter how tight I make the two bands to the boat, they slide about a bit.

The wheels will tip to the right or left depending on how much the restraining bands shift.

I am using this trolley with an Old Town Pack Canoe. Those are bit shorter and wider in middle then many canoes. Thus it is easy for the bands to shift about, especially if you plan to pull the canoe with the wheels on the back end of the canoe. Were the move over pavement or other very smooth ground, it may go well. I have to move my canoe from back of yard over uneven ground and that causes the straps to shift on one side or the other.

When strap on on side slides back, the wheels won't run true and the canoe will be pulling in that direction. This will continue until you can't pull the canoe at all and have to reset the whole thing. For a long portage, this won't work.

The second time I used this thing, I put the trolley on the front and pushed it and things went better over a short distance. It was still balking and it was not a smooth run.

Next time I use it, I will try to set the trolley in the center of canoe and see how that goes. I expect some more experimentation will result in usable solution. But, if you have a fatter canoe with more of a narrowing at front and back, have to transport over uneven ground, and want to pull the canoe instead of pushing it; there may be things may not go well.
text_fidelity_b: Bonnlo Boat Kayak Canoe Cart Carrier Dolly Trailer Tote Trolley Transport Kayak Accessories Large with 20x2mm Aluminum Pipe Double Kickstands, Inflation Free Solid Tire Wheels, 2 Ratchet Straps

text_fidelity_a: TOOGOO(R) 20 Clear Crystal Waggler Fishing Fish Floats Floating Stem Tube Set I ordered these 20 Clear Crystal Waggler Fishing Fish Floats Floating Tubes from SODIAL because they were really cheap $3.13  & FREE SHIPPING.  They are hollow plastic tubes with a glued on blaze orange top.  They float high with a small weight and baited hook.  A minnow will even be able to drag them down, in the smaller sizes.  Due to the blaze red/orange painted tops, during daylight hours they really stand out on the surface of the water.  Also, they are very noticeable as the light wanes in the evening or early hours of the day.  Without adequate weight below them, they will lay over on their side. The larger floats stand quite high off the water with small split shots for ballast. For the price, they are a pretty good buy and I think they will perform well for Crappie or sunfish.  Adult use should make them last longer, but if you bounce them around, they most likely may break or split.  The hollow tube is a soft plastic, not completely rigid or too brittle.  The bottom is where the eye is located and it can break with casting abuse.  The eye of the float will need some probing, as most are not a completely pierced hole and will need some attention with the point of a hook.  I also purchased a few packages of more meaty floats from Betts - Billy Boy Bobbers - Which are weighted and have snap on line connectors for the float assortment.  They are both, OK.

OKAI EA10 Electric Scooter with Seat, Up to 25-35 Miles Range & 15.5MPH, Moped Scooter Bike for Adults with 10 Inch Vacuum Tires Set up of the scooter is a fairly simple process. The only downside is putting on the bike seat. It doesn’t slide down very easily and isn’t fully secure, the seat swivels back and forth which can be inconvenient.

The scooter in general is great and able to take me from point A to point B in a timely manner. One feature that really makes the scooter user friendly is the battery. Being able to take the battery out and leave the scooter outside while charging it inside is extremely convenient.

The keys that come with the scooter are also extremely convenient. With the NFC feature it’s easy to unlock, all you have to do is touch the key to the scooter’s digital interface.

Making sure you have enough battery is important if you are planning on going somewhere far. The gauge on the scooter doesn’t give you an accurate idea of how far you can go, and the apps percentages aren’t very accurate either.

One other thing I wish it had was a longer pole. It is tall enough for my hand to reach it when I’m standing but it has to be fully extended so it can be awkward and unsafe. If it was a little bit longer, it’d be perfect for sitting and standing.

It is most comfortable to ride while sitting but you are able to stand. Depending on your height, standing may feel comfortable or a bit awkward. If you’re around the 6ft range it feels slightly too short to use while standing, although it is possible. It would've been nice if some adjustments have been made in the scooter so that it would have been easy to use both sitting and standing.

The scooter is really easy to operate. Right out of the box, all you do is turn it on and go. The acceleration is quick and the brakes are fast and efficient.

The scooter is made in China and being sold by Chinese company on Amazon. At the current price of 700 bucks I'm sure it's at least 250 bucks over priced.

text_fidelity_a:
SPRI Step360 Pro Trainer Essentially a marriage between Bosu and regular steppers, this device promises to bring the best of both to the home exercise routine. While it does a provide an acceptable basic workout, it does not quite make the mark.

The device itself is large and bulky. You must inflate it with a really lame hand pump. I thought the pump was flimsy. There are no valves, just holes that are plugged after inflation. Once inflated, it is essentially two firm air cushions topped with a balance board. I did find that it held its air, which was good since I do not relish another round with the hand pump. The enclosed dvd comes with instructions and workouts. If you have resistance bands, you are good to go.If not, you need to purchase some because they are not included. The workouts are basic and unlikely to challenge advanced and intermediate exercisers. Overall, this is not a terribly successful hybrid. There is some wobble but probably not enough to make a significant difference in the workout.

As tempting as this concept was, I did not find it superior to or a replacement for either my regular stepper or Bosu. Although the device itself is sturdy, the cost cutting short cuts (hand pump, no valves, no resistance bands) detract. If you are a beginner with a craving for novelty, this device might be a good choice. But overall, I thought it failed to realize its promise.
text_fidelity_b: SPRI Step360 Pro Trainer

text_fidelity_a:
Miken 2014 REV-EX YRVX12 Baseball Bat (-12) For a full review please check out generationXdad

This will be my sons last year of playing machine pitch, next year we move up to kid pitch. Last year we used an aluminum baseball bat, it wasn't bad but I did notice that kids with composite bats seemed to be hitting the ball much further.

Composite bats have a high "trampoline effect," meaning that the ball comes off faster because of the material used in the bat. When a ball hits a traditional wood bat, it gets compressed before taking off, and loses energy in the process, so it comes out more slowly. In a metal or composite bat, the bat compresses instead, so the ball retains most of its energy and flies off at a higher speed.

Additionally, the carbon fiber of composite bats actually becomes more flexible with each hit. Their ability to compress goes up, and the balls fly off faster and faster.

So this year we decided to pick up a new composite bat for the season. After reading reviews and talking to a few parents we decided to go with the Miken Rev-Ex.
If you spend a little time looking at composite bats you’ll find there’s a lot of options out there that range in price from $150 to $300+. I definitely didn’t want to spend over $200 for a baseball bat. Miken came in at the price point I was looking for. We pulled the trigger and purchased the bat from Amazon (points, points, points)

Because of this you should check with the league your child plays in and make sure that composite bats are allowed. We play in Babe Ruth, composite bats are still allowed, however Little League only allows approved bats (This bat is on their approved list).

The first day my son started using the Miken Rev-Ex I noticed a difference in how far he could hit the ball. I would guess he added a solid 20 to 30 feet in distance to his solid hits. I also notice that balls hit in the infield were like bullets! Any solid hit off this bats comes off with speed!

So far my son has been very happy with the Miken Rev-Ex and has been taken extra care of it!

Final Review: For the price and performance I’m very happy with the improvements that I have seen. I can’t speak to warranty and hope that I never need to. If you’re looking for a good fairly priced composite bat then I recommend the Miken Rev-Ex.
Being an Amazon Prime member I had the bat in two days. First thing I noticed was the warning label on the bat.
text_fidelity_b: Miken 2014 REV-EX YRVX12 Baseball Bat (-12)

Stansport Aluminum Tent Peg, 9-Inch These stakes are well-constructed and can be pounded into reasonably hard soil without damage. I haven't destroyed any yet, but I do try to be careful when I'm pounding them into rocky ground. (A small, 8-ounce hammer works well. Larger hammers increase the likelihood of bending or breaking your stakes). The round cross section doesn't have the holding power of some of the flatter stake designs, so they don't hold as well in wind, in my experience. They're longer than most other after-market tent stakes, though (9 inches vs the more common 7-inches), which helps compensate. I like to have a few of these in my stake bag for places that the y-shaped stakes can't penetrate.

Some users have complained that they can't get their tent guylines through the holes in the silver heads. That isn't how they are intended to be used. Wrap your guyline or your anchor loop around the shaft of the stake, just below the silver head, and angle your stake to point it toward a point several feet below the center of your tent. These are fine stakes. Would like to try some of this style in a longer, 12-inch version, for larger tents that catch more wind and require stronger anchors.
text_fidelity_b: Stansport Aluminum Tent Peg, 9-Inch

Portable Camping Water Purifier Dual 0.01 Micron Water Filtration System for Outdoor Backpacking, Hiking, Emergency - Dual Filters Version My son is the gizmo kid. He is always coming home with some sort of set up to try out some new intricate system whether it be electronics or board game development or survival gear. When he was starting to come home and excitedly show me his solar panels, battery collection devices for long term storage and charging and all of his plans to create a little camping area, I knew this would be great for him.

CHARGING
This does have to be charged, but knowing that he already had rigged up some sort of charging world with his solar panels and battery storage I did not think it would be a problem for him- which it isn't. He already explained a few ways to charge it in his system.

DOES IT WORK?
Getting details out of my son is not an easy feat. However, this works well, tastes good, and if you are prepared to wash it out now and then if you use really dirty water, you can keep it running well.

TASTE
He prefers not to use really muddy water, so that test is not one that really matters to him, but having water from a nearby pond or stream where he camps from time to time works well for this. The taste is good and he is happy.

IS IT HARD TO USE?
If this was too hard to use, he would not be using it. I would say that this is pretty straightforward and not difficult. You just have to air it out in between uses if you are not regularly running it.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This water purification system is great for camping or emergencies, as long as you have battery back up to charge it from if there is no power.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This has worked well for what my son wants it for and he seems happy with it. If we ever do need to use it in an emergency situation, I could try to update, but at that point, internet most likely won't be working anyway. LOL.

Assembly was straightforward and without any issues. In use, it seems well made and sturdy. It's a typical flywheel design with a knob to adjust a resistance onto the wheel itself. The seat is completely adjustable for height and can be position more forward or rearward to further adjust your position relative to the pedals and the handlebars. It uses a standard bicycle seat, so that should be an easy thing to do.

The pedals are those "steel trap" type with the jagged contacts that require you to wear shoes. I'm okay with that, but theres a nylon strap system that surrounds your toes. My size 12 feet means I'm pedaling on my toes. The pedals, therefore, were the first thing to be replaced. Again, it uses standard picycly parts so replacement was easy.

The control module is a simple battery operated counter. It can track miles, calories or time... or it can be set to cycle through the various measurements as you go. Theres no connection to the adjustable wheel resistance, so things like calorie burn are obviously just an approximation, at best. But that's pretty typical, I'm sure.

Overall, I recommend this bike. It seems well made and it gets the job done.

Stealth Core Pro Trainer - Get Strong Sexy Abs and Lean Core Playing Games On Your Phone; Free iOS/Android App; 4 Free Mobile Games Included; Dynamic Abs & Core Training; Only 3 Minutes a Day, Pro Commercial Gym Quality (Orange) Yes, this is a gimmick, but in this case the gimmick is the best feature.

Sure, I can do a normal plank for free. It only takes access to a flat surface. But I don't. This I go for multiple times a day because it's fun. The gamification, makes me actually do the exercise and that alone makes it worth it for me.

If you're the "can't break the streak" type, this has what you want.

It you're the "I need to be distracted during planks" type (like me) this has you covered. The time flies.

If you want this to make planks harder, A-you're nuts. Planks are hard enough and B-this won't do anything by itself to add resistance to the plank. It glides very easily. There are videos on the website you might like though.

There are two free games. I keep playing the glider one which, if I'm doing it right, involves repeatedly crashing into trees. I'm reasonably certain I'm not doing it right. The other is a space game. Or, for $30 a year, you can get access to a whole whack more games. They do countdown (set a time you want to plank and have the timer automatically increase every day) or count up (go as long as you can). I like countdown, personally, with a little more of a challenge every day.

Definitely join the Facebook community. The folk are upbeat, encouraging, and amazing. There is a lot of good information to be had there as well.

I didn't expect to like this quite so much, and I honestly feared I'd regret the purchase (I was really on the fence with this) so I'm pleasantly surprised to find I love it.

text_fidelity_a: Schwinn Fitness 430 Elliptical Trainer [Discontinued] Before making this purchase, I did my homework in reading reviews and trying out several other ellipticals at fitness stores. It relatively compact and has a nice smooth motion to the stride.  It did start to squeak a day or two after we bought and assembled it. It doesn't have a lot of the extra bells and whistles such as an ipod connection or a fan, but those items could be introduced externally.  Also the monitor is a little difficult to read. text_fidelity_a: Cammenga Official US Military Tritium Lensatic Compass, Accurate Waterproof Hand Held Compasses with Pouch for Hiking Camping Navigation Survival Backpacking Orienteering My husband has been looking at this compass for awhile.  So, I decided to order it for him for Father's Day. On the day I expected to receive it, instead I got a clear bag from (USPS), the post office. Inside was the pristine padded Prime bag that Amazon had sent the compass in. On the outside of the USPS bag was an apology it also stated the content of the Amazon bag was damaged. I looked at the Amazon bag it looked perfect, no gouges, no scrapes or tears on the outside. I thought how did the compass get damaged, if the bag isn't? Then I noticed the Amazon bag had a perfect cut across the top and then I looked inside, there was nothing - empty! Where is the damaged compass?Then I look at the USPS bag again and read the outside a second time. Just an apology no instructions as what to do. Am I just out the money I spent and now I have no gift too? I contacted Amazon customer service and the representative assured me the compass would be replaced at no cost to me. She told me luckily, that I had contacted them early enough to have the replacement compass sent out that very day. She said she would initiate an investigation, as I requested. This was with tax was nearly a hundred dollar item. I am thankful that they are, as when things are apparently stolen,  it hurts all of us on the cost of things. Amazon, like all companies, can't stay in business, if they are giving away items. I received the replacement compass in plenty of time for a gift on Father's Day. He loves it, it works perfectly. He wanted it because of being able to read it in total darkness. He can't  wait until the fall when he can use it when hunting. Thanks Amazon!
text_fidelity_b: Cammenga Official US Military Tritium Lensatic Compass, Accurate Waterproof Hand Held Compasses with Pouch for Hiking Camping Navigation Survival Backpacking Orienteering

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in)) I want so badly to give this 5-stars. I am settling with 3 for now. Here's why:
Pros-
This is my first fitness tracker. I like that it measures my heart beat and steps- the exercise mode is nice too. I LOVE that I can sync it with my phone to have a vibrated notification of calls/caller ID and that it also does silent alarms. These features have been quickly integrated into my daily routine and I LOVE them!

Cons-
My first complaint comes about the mobile app. I have an android phone. My son has the CHARGE fitbit, and for some reason his app tells how long it takes him to fall asleep (minor difference, I will admit, but...) the app, while displaying the stats info from your tracker, as well as compiling averages for periods of time, doesn't give suggestions on how to modify your routine. The website offers a "premium" service, which gives you more detailed analysis, but I'm not sure it will also provide those missing helpful suggestions.
My second, and biggest complaint is the battery. I saw one reviewer experienced a similar issue with their fitbit and I can say after a mere 9 days of use, I can barely go 24hrs without a low battery notice, it's going back. I have been in touch with fitbit customer support today, and they seem to.be on top of things, but if I don't get a response I'm happy with, I'll have to try something else. My son has a refurbished fitbit charge, and it is working VERY well. I wanted us to be able to continue to run challenges ( he's 9, so keeping up with his 12,000 steps a day is an EXCELLENT GOAL for me!) But if I have to switch brands, I guess I will. Will update this review as soon as something changes!

Update! 11 months later:
I am so disappointed with my entire fitbit experience. I purchased another HR finding a better deal elsewhere after my original band quit working on me and I returned it to amazon. I should have quit while I was ahead. I have had 3 replacements, first 2 had issues with the internal functions and quit working. The 3rd fell apart. I do not wear in the shower, avoid getting it wet, or leaving damp after sweating even a little. I finally gave up and asked fitbit to do something- their response, I could have ANOTHER charge hr OR throw away my original $$$ and purchase ANOTHER Fitbit product at 30% off. Seriously?! I didn't have any of the trackers for more than 4 months each and they wanted me to replace their failed product by PAYING MORE for a replacement. No way! Throughly disgusted. Please, if you don't have disposable income to keep paying to replace these, look elsewhere.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in))

Garmin fēnix 5, Premium and Rugged Multisport GPS Smartwatch, Granite Blue Functionally speaking, this watch is pretty full featured. It has basic mapping and will accomodate most common activities very well. I like the build quality as well. I don't use any of the health monitoring features, so those are disabled to save battery life. Battery life is OK overall, not great. It loses about 8-10% on a one hour hike.

The reason for the one star review has to do with the non-replaceable battery, and the fact that this is a $500+ watch. I am on year two of owning this watch now and have seen about a 30% drop in battery life. That's pretty bad if you ask me. I predict I'll get another couple years out of it before the battery becomes unreliable for anything more than a run around the neighborhood. As such I can't recommend this watch at all as I think it is a very poor value... 3-5 years of use for a watch that costs upwards of $1000 for the high end models is totally unacceptable.

I've got an old Forerunner 101 that I bought back in the early 2000s that I prefer over the Fenix. It's comically bulky, but runs on AAA batteries, so you can just keep going and going and going. I wish Garmin would have kept the Forerunner line.

So, I've launched 'new concept' products in high tech. I should have recalled a prime reason for initial failure to launch … crap tech pubs instructions. I would guess that the instructions were 'outsourced'. Missing in the instructions is the operational concept. The order of the instructions is not typical Western operational logic. The instructions need a serious rewrite. The tech pub writer missed the boat. I figured it picking up 'Why the silicone quality of the whole top?'.

Weighted Jump Rope - (1LB) Solid PVC for Crossfit and Boxing - Heavy Jump Rope with Memory Non-Slip Cushioned Foam Grip Handles for Fitness Workouts Endurance and Strength Training Life recently changed and as I searched for ways to stay in shape I found an old cheap jump rope in the closet. After 3 weeks of trying, with some moderate success, I realized that the rope I was using was holding me back. I needed a longer, heavier, sturdier rope.
I spent a good amount of time comparing reviews. I just got back from a workout with this product.

1. The rope is easily adjustable. I am 6'4" and it is a good height for me, but others who are average height will need to adjust. You will need basic tools (phillips screw driver and strong cutters), but you can always ask a handy friend or family member to help.
2. The rope is thick, and the handles are large. They work perfectly for me, but if you have small hands or issues with hand/joint pain you may want to take that into consideration.
3. The product is made out of good quality plastic. It shows signs of wearing from the first use, but that is to be expected. I would warn people to be careful and not throw this on the ground, the handles would likely easily crack/break or cause gouges out of the plastic that could be painful on your hands.
4. The rope is 1.5 pounds, and the weight is in the ROPE.
5. The rope performs well, is sturdy, and offers good swing and feedback. You can easily slow down or speed up as you're jumping, and the rope keeps a nice arc even on windy days.
6. One reviewer said this left red marks on their legs, I don't see how anyone could do that with this rope without some intention. It does weigh 1.5 pounds though and is fast, so be careful of your surroundings.

Overall this is a good purchase and addition to my isolation routine. I wanted a solid $30 option, and this product fit the bill.

text_fidelity_a:
Hip Hop Abs DVD Workout I was recently lucky enough to find this entire 3-DVD set at a used book sale. However, I almost passed it up--I already owned [[ASIN:B00GW5RTU6 Shaun T's Hip Hop Abs 2]], a second, more advanced version of this set, so I thought that maybe I didn't need the original. However, I decided to purchase the set anyway--I thought maybe I would pass it along to my sister, but as it turns out, I love these workouts and am keeping this set for myself!

Hip Hop Abs is led by Shaun T, who is a fun, motivating--albeit at times goofy--instructor. He teaches all of the workouts live with a group of 6-8 background exercisers (or 2-3 for the "Last Minute" workouts), one of whom, Tania, always shows low-impact modifications for the few higher impact moves that are occasionally thrown in. Shaun's mirrored cuing is excellent, and he frequently offers helpful form pointers, although they sometimes come in the midst of his raps/rhymes. I've provided breakdowns for all of the workouts in this set below.

***DISC 1***

SECRETS TO FLAT ABS
In this section, Shaun runs through basic form principles used throughout his Hip Hop Abs (HHA) workouts, which he calls the "tilt, tuck, tighten" method. Tilt involves tilting the shoulders forward over the hips; tuck means to tuck the pelvis forward; and tighter involves pulling in the stomach and breathing out as if blowing out a candle. He uses several simple exercises to practice these basics.

FAT BURNING CARDIO (30 mins)
This cardio routine begins with a 4-minute warm-up that includes side-to-side steps, slides, pumps forward and back, and some simple stretches. The first combo, "Party Bounce," is about 6.5 minutes and consists largely of variations on the basic pump. Next is the "Night Fever" combo (6 mins), which offers the throw-down, grapevine, press the floor, and a double arm pull-down. This is followed by the "Get Busy" combo (6 mins). Exercises included are the uprock (heels forward), the get busy sequence, and roll out. The last combination is the 4.5-minute "Freak Out." This starts with kick it and then moves into the "Freak" side step, with several different variations of this. The 2-minute cool-down is QUICK: Shaun takes a few breaths and then moves through some brief stretches for the lower back and neck.

BONUS: CARDIO GROOVE (40 mins + optional 6 mins)
I was surprised to find this workout on the disc, as it is not listed on the DVD case. It is another cardio routine, but with some twists. For example, the 3-minute warm-up includes some new moves such as robo arms. The first cardio segment (7.5 mins) starts with a basic bounce and then moves into a party walk/run, rock hi/lo, and rainbow step. The next cardio sequence is longer at 11.5 minutes, and it includes two bounces side, party stomp, push it, and hammer roll. This is followed by the "Party Hop" combo, which includes moves such as dig, run hop, kick it, and get busy (adding a jump). Finally, there is another longer (9.5 mins) segment, "Party Slick": this features the basic bounce, criss-cross, Afro slide, smooth walk. Shaun T concludes with a very brief (1.5 mins) cool-down stretch. At the end of the main workout, there is a "Cardio Groove Challenge" segment. In this 6-minute sequence, Shaun performance ALL of the above moves twice through in a "take it from the top" (aka TIFTT) fashion.

***DISC 2***

AB SCUPLT (24.5 mins)
This is a cardio workout that even more specifically targets the abs. Moves include roll in, flava jam, and oblique hip flexor flava; light weights are also used for twists, hands up, and get busy. With 6.5 minutes remaining in the routine, Shaun T moves to the mat for several moves in a c-curve position (c-jam, c-flava, bow & arrow), and then he concludes the workout with a 2-minute stretch on the floor.

TOTAL BODY BURN (41.5 mins)
This routine has both cardio and light toning benefits. The 4.5-minute warm-up is similar to the Fat Burning Cardio warm-up; Shaun concludes with some stretching lunges. He then moves into what he calls "3-tier squats" (3.5 mins), or squats performed in different positions and at different tempos. Next is the "hoop," a side-to-side twist adding a knee (3.5 mins). An 8-minute series using light weights (or weighted gloves) follows; exercises here include party walk, party combo, and raise the roof. Shaun also uses the weights for an overhead press and standing abs crunch. This is followed by a 5-minute "Cardio Burn" segment which includes freak, Afro arms, and frat step. Going back to the weights, Shaun performs a short sequence for biceps and triceps (2.5 mins), and then a slightly longer (4 mins) series which includes more standing abs work. With 9.5 minutes left in the routine, Shaun moves to the floor for 5 minutes of plank work (low plank, pulses, push-ups, full plank, plank leg lifts). He also does a very brief (<2 minutes) abs sequence which includes twists, superman, and knee ups. Shaun concludes the workout with 2.5 minutes of stretches performed both on the back and on the stomach.

LAST MINUTE ABS (5 minutes)
This quick workout starts with a roll-in variation and moves into oblique work ("Flo-rique") involving various knee lifts and arm moves. A hammer leg lift is performed to the front, and to the side, and the workout concludes with a superman bounce and roll.

BONUS - LEARN TO DANCE: TAKE IT TO THE DANCE FLOOR

***DISC 3***

HIPS, BUNS, & THIGHS (25 mins)
This is a cardio workout with more of an emphasis on the lower body. There is a short (1.5 mins) warm-up to start which includes a step tap with a dip low. The "Lower Body Groove" includes "Let's Rock," a heel/toe move, squats, standing crunch, lunge dips, pelvic tilts front/back, and side leg lifts with squats. With 8 minutes remaining, Shaun moves the the mat for some all-4s work (5 mins), including push backs, straight leg lifts, holds, L lifts, and bent leg lifts. The 2.5-minute stretch starts seated and moves to lying for a hip flexor stretch, sphinx, cobra, and down dog before returning to standing.

LAST MINUTE BUNS (7 mins)
This is a brief but intense segment focused on the lower body. Shaun starts with several squat variations, including the funky squat, pulse squat, and jump squat. Next, he moves through the funky lunge and jump lunge. This is followed by some standing glute work and runs. There is no warm-up or cool-down for this routine, so it's best used as an add-on.

BONUS - LEARN TO DANCE: HIP HOP GROOVE

As noted above, I really enjoy these workouts. I own over 100 fitness DVDs (and have tried MANY more), and I think Shaun T really stands out as an instructor who is able to offer cardio routines that are interesting, intense (my heart rate is always elevated doing HHA) yet still mostly low impact (the few hops and other higher impact moves are easily modified if desired). Plus, the cardio is completely doable; there is no learning curve here (a must for me!). Given these factors, HHA is likely to appeal to a wide range of exercisers, from those who are more intermediate/advanced like myself to more beginning level exercisers who can utilize the shorter routines and modify where needed. I am thoroughly enjoying this DVD set and would definitely recommend it to others!
text_fidelity_b: Hip Hop Abs DVD Workout

text_fidelity_a: RockyMounts Hendrix Compact Folding Bicycle Lock This is an interesting bicycle lock. It weighs about 1.5 pounds and folds up to the size of a water bottle. It unfolds to about the same size as a standard U-lock and can lock your bike in most places where you could use a U-lock. There is enough space to lock your frame and rear wheel to a bike rack. U-locks are 2 pounds and up, so this lock saves weight and is smaller and easier to carry. It is certainly more secure than any cable lock which are always easy to cut with hand tools. The steel plates are not real thick (about 3mm), but because of their width, I have to imagine they are safer than a lightweight slightly thicker chain lock when attacked by bolt cutters. I do worry about how safe the joints are. The manufacturer claims a safety rating of 7/10, but this is their own rating, there is no industry standard rating system in the USA.
